headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Khoj reads indexed personal notes and uses broad network egress, while Dagster has no filesystem or network access, making prompt-injection and capability-conflict risks low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly feed content into Khoj. Khoj does read indexed files and can use web search, but the pair lacks a documented automatic bridge. The only plausible pathway is unusual manual transfer or external orchestration, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Dagster output into Khoj chat or notes, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared external workspace is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting Dagster-generated text into Khoj without review.
Disable any shared note-sync or export/import bridge.
Use a human review step before Khoj acts on imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no egress, but Khoj reads personal notes/files and can send queries to a Khoj cloud or configured search providers. Because the pair lacks a shared filesystem in the profiles, leakage is not automatic, yet Khoj's default retrieval and network paths can expose indexed documents if sensitive notes are present.
conditions: IF sensitive notes are indexed in Khoj and a cloud or external search provider is configured, those contents may leave the local environment.
IF Dagster outputs are manually imported into Khoj's indexed documents, they become subject to Khoj retrieval and egress paths.
mitigations: Index only non-sensitive notes in Khoj.
Use self-hosted providers only.
Review and prune the indexed document set.
Separate Dagster artifacts from Khoj's note corpus.
Turn off external search providers for sensitive sessions.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP, while Khoj also cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource in the profiles, there is no plausible capability conflict pathway.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to grant shared write access to the same directory, this verdict no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared artifacts.
Do not grant shared git or database credentials.
Recheck the profiles before enabling any write-capable plugin.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is an orchestrator that can produce pipeline outputs, and Khoj is a conversational retrieval agent that may present retrieved content as answers. The profiles do not show a verification gate between them, so if Dagster output is imported into Khoj, Khoj may treat it as authoritative and propagate errors. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Dagster-generated text is ingested into Khoj without validation, Khoj may echo or act on incorrect facts.
IF Khoj is used to summarize Dagster outputs for downstream action, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require source citations before Khoj reuses Dagster output.
Add a manual verification step for any Dagster-derived facts.
Label Dagster artifacts as untrusted input in Khoj.
Restrict Khoj from taking external actions on summarized results.

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster is open-source and shows no touched data classes, while Khoj explicitly handles personal notes, indexed documents, and model-provider API keys. If personal notes include regulated or residency-bound data, Khoj's cloud or configured search-provider calls can create a compliance mismatch. Dagster is not the main compliance surface here, so it is not cited beyond its lack of data handling.
conditions: IF regulated personal notes are indexed in Khoj and routed to a cloud provider or external search service, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF model-provider API keys are used in a jurisdiction with stricter logging rules, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Khoj indexes.
Use a self-hosted deployment with documented retention settings.
Review provider contracts and data-processing terms.
Rotate and scope API keys narrowly.
Delete any sensitive indexed documents before enabling external search.
